The name is also linked to various forts and temples dedicated to local deities, such as Jain Tirthankaras, accepted protectors of the community.

historical_references.reference: The name Dungar is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Durg', meaning fort or protective wall. It was the name of a hill fort located in the Sahyadri hills, in present day Maharashtra, India. This fort was strategically important during the Maratha Empire, as it controlled the trade route between the Deccan and the Konkan regions.

Another reference to the name Dungar can be found in the Hindu epic 'Mahabharata'. In this text, Dungar is described as a mountain located near the Himalayas, where the goddess Parvati performed severe penance to please Lord Shiva. The name Dungar is said to mean 'difficult to reach' or 'inaccessible' due to its steep and rugged terrain.
